raw_response:
I will not spread my 6 mu too thin. I only farmed one year, so I will mostly follow what I saw nearby that gave a steady harvest. I will keep 3 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because around here that is the safest way to keep grain in hand. I will put 2 mu into cotton and 1 mu into stevia, just to leave some cash crop money, but I will not push too much land into the crops I know less well. I do not like taking chances with fertilizer. If I am unsure, I will put a little more rather than a little less, because losing yield hurts more than wasting one bag. For wheat I will plough, put the base fertilizer in, water about 3 times with my well, and keep the stand even. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize on the same 3 mu with no-tillage, because that saves labor and catches the season. Cotton needs more watching, so I will spray more times there. Stevia is smaller area, so I will manage it by hand and keep water on it when it turns hot. I will do the work in the simple way I can finish with family labor and a little hired help only if the busy days pile up.
